body.p: The Git Client add-on supports HTTPS and SSH connections to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and other Git servers. It also supports ssh-agent forwarding.
body.note:
For SSH connections, the Use SSH Agent option is enabled by default, so the Git Client can use keys already stored in the SSH agent. To check or change this option, go to
Git Settings Preferences SSH Connections . You can also open the Ellipsis menu in the Git Staging view toolbar and select
Preferences SSH Connections .
body.p: To access a remote repository, provide your authentication details, unless you use unprotected SSH keys. If the add-on does not find stored authentication details, it prompts you for them.

For HTTPS connections, the Git Client add-on supports basic authentication and personal access tokens.
GitHub no longer accepts password-based authentication.
Authentication with personal access tokens has been tested with GitHub and GitLab.
As of September 9, 2025, Bitbucket app passwords can no longer be created. Use API tokens with scopes instead. Provide the API token as the password for Basic authentication, along with the correct Bitbucket username.

If two-factor authentication (2FA) is enabled for GitHub or GitLab, generate a personal access token for your profile. Then, in the Git Staging view in , use the generated token value as the authentication password when prompted for credentials.

If you switch to another account on the same Git server, reset your credentials so that the Git Client prompts you for new ones. Only one set of credentials is stored for each Git server. To reset your credentials, open the Ellipsis menu in the Git Staging view toolbar and select Reset all credentials.
